The Prophet forbade travelling to a hostile country carrying copies of the Quran.
Uthman had Zaid bin Thabit and three Quraishis copy the Quran, telling them to write in the language of Quraish where they differed, as it was revealed in it.
Umar calls Ubai the best reciter yet leaves some of his statements, since Ubai keeps all he heard though Allah says He abrogates verses or causes them to be forgotten.
The Prophet recited the verse on the Book's clear and unclear verses and warned against those who follow the unclear ones, saying Allah named them as deviating.
After Yamama, Abu Bakr, urged by Umar, had Zaid bin Thabit collect the Quran from writings and memories, finding two verses of At-Tauba only with Khuza'ima.
While collecting the Quran into copies, Zaid bin Thabit found a missing verse of Surat al-Ahzab only with Khuzaima, whose witness the Prophet counted as two men's.
Ubai bin Ka'b, told that Ibn Mas'ud excluded the two surahs of refuge, says the Prophet told him they were revealed to him and he recited them.
After Yamama Abu Bakr has Zaid bin Thabit collect the Quran; Uthman sends a copy to every province and has other copies burnt; Zaid also wrote verses for the Prophet.
Aisha explains why a surah mentioning Paradise and the Fire came before laws, and dictates the surahs in order; companions name surahs learnt early and paired surahs the Prophet recited.
Ibn Abbas and Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyya say the Prophet left nothing except what is between the two bindings of the Quran.
After many Quran reciters fell at Al-Yamama, Abu Bakr, urged by Umar, had Zaid bin Thabit collect the Quran from scattered writings and men's memories.
Sent by Abu Bakr to collect the Quran, Zaid bin Thabit found the last verses of Surat at-Tauba with Abu Khuzaima Al-Ansari alone.
